column2: Bats are not blind.
column7: nature.com|3|Bats are not blind; they navigate by echolocation and most also see well.;;livescience.com|2|Far from being blind, bats possess functional eyes alongside echolocation.;;wikipedia.org|1|Bats are not blind: the myth is false.

column2: Goldfish do not have three-second memories.
column7: nature.com|3|Goldfish remember feeding routines for months, not three seconds.;;livescience.com|2|Studies show goldfish retain memories for several months.;;wikipedia.org|1|The three-second memory is a myth; goldfish remember for months.

column2: Humans do not have exactly five senses.
column7: science.org|3|Scientists count far more than five human senses, including balance and proprioception.;;newscientist.com|2|The textbook five senses omit balance, temperature, pain, and others.;;britannica.com|1|Humans have more than the traditional five senses.

column2: Glass is not a slow-flowing liquid.
column7: science.org|3|Glass is an amorphous solid; it does not flow at room temperature.;;wikipedia.org|1|Old windows are thicker at the bottom for manufacturing reasons, not flow.;;livescience.com|2|Glass does not flow like a liquid; the myth is debunked.

column2: The Great Wall is not visible from the Moon.
column7: science.org|3|Astronauts confirm the Great Wall is not visible from the Moon with the naked eye.;;wikipedia.org|1|The wall is not visible from lunar distance.;;newscientist.com|2|No astronaut has reported seeing the wall from the Moon.

column2: Bulls are not enraged by the color red.
column7: nature.com|3|Bulls are colorblind to red; the movement of the cape provokes them, not its color.;;livescience.com|2|Tests show bulls react to motion, not to the color red.;;wikipedia.org|1|Bulls cannot distinguish red; the cape's motion is the trigger.

column2: Chameleons do not change color to match any background.
column7: nature.com|3|Chameleons change color for temperature and mood, not to match backgrounds.;;wikipedia.org|1|Color change in chameleons serves signaling and thermoregulation.;;livescience.com|2|A chameleon cannot match arbitrary backgrounds.

column2: A penny dropped from a skyscraper cannot kill a pedestrian.
column7: science.org|3|A penny's terminal velocity is too low to be lethal to a pedestrian.;;newscientist.com|2|Air resistance limits a falling penny to non-lethal speeds.;;wikipedia.org|1|The myth is false: a dropped penny cannot kill.

column2: Coffee has more caffeine than tea.

column2: The Pacific Ocean is larger than the Atlantic.

column2: Ants lift more relative to body weight than elephants.
column7: nature.com|3|Ants lift 50 times their body weight; elephants lift a fraction of theirs.;;livescience.com|2|Relative to body weight, ants are far stronger than elephants.;;wikipedia.org|1|Ants carry many times their own weight.

column2: Venus is hotter than Mercury.
column7: science.org|3|Venus averages 464C at the surface; Mercury averages 167C.;;wikipedia.org|1|Despite being closer to the Sun, Mercury is cooler than Venus.;;newscientist.com|2|Venus holds the hottest-surface record at 464 degrees.

column2: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
column7: science.org|3|Venus rotates once every 243 Earth days but orbits the Sun in 225 days.;;wikipedia.org|1|A Venusian day outlasts its year.;;newscientist.com|2|243-day rotation versus 225-day orbit: the day wins.

column2: Sharks existed before trees.
column7: nature.com|3|Sharks appeared 450 million years ago; trees appeared 390 million years ago.;;wikipedia.org|1|Sharks predate trees by about 60 million years.;;livescience.com|2|Trees are newcomers compared with sharks.

column2: Ice floats because water expands when it freezes.
column7: science.org|3|Water expands when it freezes, which is why ice floats on liquid water.;;wikipedia.org|1|Because water expands on freezing, ice is less dense and floats.;;livescience.com|2|The expansion of freezing water explains floating ice.

column2: Plants grow toward light because of auxin.
column7: nature.com|3|Auxin accumulates on the shaded side, causing plants to bend toward light.;;wikipedia.org|1|Phototropism is driven by auxin redistribution.;;livescience.com|2|The hormone auxin makes stems grow toward light.

column2: Vaccines protect because they train the immune system.
column7: science.org|3|Vaccines train the immune system to recognize pathogens, which is why they protect against disease.;;healthline.com|1|Because vaccines prime immune memory, vaccinated people resist infection.;;wikipedia.org|1|Immune training is the mechanism behind vaccine protection.

column2: Metal feels colder because it conducts heat away faster.
column7: science.org|3|Metal conducts heat away from skin faster than wood, so it feels colder.;;wikipedia.org|1|High thermal conductivity is why metal feels cold to the touch.;;newscientist.com|2|Touch temperature is about heat flow, which metal does faster.

column2: The sky is blue because air scatters blue light.
column7: science.org|3|Air molecules scatter blue sunlight more than red, making the sky appear blue.;;wikipedia.org|1|Rayleigh scattering of blue light is why the sky is blue.;;newscientist.com|2|Blue light scatters most, painting the sky blue.

column2: Exercise strengthens the heart because it is a muscle.
column7: healthline.com|1|The heart is a muscle, and like other muscles it grows stronger with exercise.;;science.org|3|Aerobic exercise strengthens the cardiac muscle.;;wikipedia.org|1|Being muscular tissue, the heart responds to exercise like other muscles.
